doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Claire Roquemore, the Detroit trumpeter, and Kenny Burrell
summary: Fuller praises Claire Roquemore as a great trumpeter who never reaped the benefit, and says Kenny Burrell put him in musical situations.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Now, another thing you’ve mentioned in passing, and I’ve heard as a Detroit player that people have a lot of respect for is Claire Roquemore.

Beautiful player. Yeah, he would give Donald Byrd, Miles Davis and all the rest of them a run for their money. He was the trumpet player that never got any significance. He never reaped any benefits from it.
Was that because of the personal lifestyle issues?

Well, he met his true mate, a girl. He was a handsome kid from a mixed family. Like I said, he was a tan complexion. He didn’t really, like Kenny Burrell and all, he didn’t really get down. You notice that Kenny didn’t get into the Grant Green thing. He was always with the vibe. But, Kenny would go to bat with me and put me in every musical situation he could before he left. He left to go on with Oscar Peterson.
